question: do the TFs bound at a distal element, weighted by whether those TFs are causal for the gene in K562 Perturb-seq, predict a CRISPR-validated enhancer-gene link better than distance and better than accessibility?

decision_threshold_stated_before_numbers.rule: all three must hold; failing (i) = no increment, failing (ii) = reads the gene and the distance, failing (iii) = reads TF density not TF identity

ground_truth.source: EP CRISPR benchmark (EngreitzLab/CRISPR_comparison), K562 arm: EPCrisprBenchmark_combined_data.training_K562.GRCh38.tsv.gz + K562 rows of EPCrisprBenchmark_combined_data.heldout_5_cell_types.GRCh38.tsv.gz

distance_x_accessibility.label: SWAP matched on distance decile x accessibility decile

degree_matched.label: SWAP additionally matched on n-TFs-bound decile (DEGREE-MATCHED)

distance_x_accessibility_TFCarm.label: SWAP matched on distance decile x accessibility decile

degree_matched_TFCarm.label: SWAP additionally matched on n-TFs-bound decile (DEGREE-MATCHED)

verdict: NO INCREMENT FROM TF CAUSALITY OVER DISTANCE AND ACCESSIBILITY -- NOT DETECTED. On 11,545 powered distal K562 CRISPR pairs at a 0.0396 positive base rate, chromosome-held-out AUPRC is 0.2786 for distance alone, 0.0829 for accessibility alone, 0.0744 for gene responsiveness with no element information at all, and 0.3587 for distance + accessibility + TF causality over 507 TFs. The full model is +0.0063 AUPRC against the best baseline (dist+acc+TFoccupancy, 0.3524), clearing the prespecified 0.010 bar in only 2/5 chromosome partitions. Weighting an element's bound TFs by whether those TFs are causal for the gene in Perturb-seq does not add to what distance and accessibility already say. The element swap is reported anyway and is consistent: a decile-matched decoy element reproduces 65% of the full model's AUPRC (0.2346 vs 0.3587, real winning 100% of 20 draws), which is what a model that reads the gene and the distance rather than the element looks like. This is a null and the project commits it.
limits: same cell line on both sides. TF->gene causality is Replogle K562 Perturb-seq and the ground truth is CRISPRi enhancer perturbation in K562. The experiments differ (gene knockdown vs element silencing, different labs and libraries), so this is not scoring a K562 layer on K562 Perturb-seq, but 'which genes move easily in K562' is shared between them. That nuisance is what the gene-responsiveness-only arm (0.0744 AUPRC with NO element information) measures and what the element swap removes. There is no RPE1 enhancer-CRISPR benchmark to escape to.

the benchmark's K562 arm is EIGHT screens with different libraries, distance ranges and hit rates. Dataset is NOT a matching key here (the swap matches on distance and accessibility deciles), so a decoy can come from a different screen than its target pair. Distance decile absorbs most of that because the screens differ mainly in distance range, but not all of it.

one ChIP file per TF (lowest-accession GRCh38 'conservative IDR thresholded peaks'). A TF whose K562 experiments disagree is represented by one of them, and 12 ChIP-profiled TFs are dropped for having no Replogle perturbation.

507 TFs is a large but not exhaustive slice of the ~1,600 human TFs; an element's real driver may be a TF with no K562 ChIP track, which would make its TF-causality features look empty for a reason that is about ENCODE's coverage and not about the element.
occupancy is binary at ELEMENT_PAD=250 bp around the tested element. Peak strength is discarded, so a marginal peak and a summit-in-the-middle peak count the same.

'causal' is |robust z| >= 5.0 in a pseudobulk knockdown. It is a CONSEQUENCE of removing the TF, direct or not -- bound_causal.py's own finding is that only ~12% of causal edges are bound at the promoter, so most of these weights are downstream effects that happen to be attached to a TF that also sits at this element.

the swap donor pool is the benchmark's own 4,362 elements. That is deliberate (a decoy that is a real tested candidate is a harder control than a random genomic window) but it means the control asks 'is THIS element better than ANOTHER TESTED element', not 'better than random DNA'.
pairs below PowerAtEffectSize25 0.8 are excluded, not counted as negatives, because not-detected is not not-linked. 234 pairs are dropped that way.
AUPRC is pooled over out-of-fold predictions within a seed. Folds are whole chromosomes, so fold sizes are uneven and a single large chromosome carries disproportionate weight in every partition.

a decoy element is required to be on a different chromosome from the gene, which removes the risk that the decoy genuinely regulates the gene but also means the swap changes chromosome-level context (replication timing, compartment) along with the element.

the model is one gradient-boosting configuration, fixed across all arms rather than tuned per arm. A tuned baseline could beat an untuned full model or the reverse; holding it fixed is what makes the arms comparable, and it means no arm is at its ceiling.
